name: chat.postEphemeral
purpose: Sends an ephemeral message to a user in a channel.

as_user.desc: (Legacy) Pass true to post the message as the authed user. Defaults to true if the chat:write:bot scope is not included. Otherwise, defaults to false.

attachments.desc: A JSON-based array of structured attachments, presented as a URL-encoded string.

blocks.desc: A JSON-based array of structured blocks, presented as a URL-encoded string.

channel.desc: Channel, private group, or IM channel to send message to. Can be an encoded ID, or a name.

icon_emoji.desc: Emoji to use as the icon for this message. Overrides icon_url.

icon_url.desc: URL to an image to use as the icon for this message.

link_names.desc: Find and link channel names and usernames.

markdown_text.desc: Accepts message text formatted in markdown. This argument should not be used in conjunction with blocks or text. Limit this field to 12,000 characters.

metadata.desc: JSON object with an entities array of work object entity metadata, presented as a URL-encoded string. Only entity metadata is supported: ephemeral messages are not persisted and never dispatch message_metadata_* events, so event_type/event_payload message metadata is ignored here. Each entity requires entity_type, entity_payload, external_ref, and url.

parse.desc: Change how messages are treated. Defaults to none. See below.

text.desc: How this field works and whether it is required depends on other fields you use in your API call. See below for more detail.

thread_ts.desc: Provide another message's ts value to post this message in a thread. Avoid using a reply's ts value; use its parent's value instead. Ephemeral messages in threads are only shown if there is already an active thread.

user.desc: id of the user who will receive the ephemeral message. The user should be in the channel specified by the channel argument.

safety_note_for_agents: This catalog documents Slack's UNDOCUMENTED/internal API surface for a specific workspace (Hack Club, Enterprise Grid). Calling an undocumented method with params_known=false means you would be guessing params against a real backend with unknown side effects -- do not do this against a real account/token without a human in the loop, and never call anything shaped like a write (*.delete, *.set, *.remove, *.create, *.update, and similar) without explicit human confirmation and a clear understanding of the blast radius, even when params_known=true.
